bullets.title: META Muse disintermediation: SHOP, EXPE, CART hit; Mizuho sees SHOP as buy
bullets.body: EXPE fell 7.7% and CART -3.3% after announcing Meta Muse partnerships, with markets pricing disintermediation risk. Mizuho pushes back on SHOP (down ~7%): wallets like Meta Pay are front-end methods, not processors — Shopify remains the underlying settlement layer at standard take rates, and management confirmed no economic change; agentic commerce is a distribution tailwind. JPM notes META Muse disintermediation basket broadly under pressure.

bullets.title: Pure Storage (P): FY28 guidance blows away consensus — 39-45% revenue growth targeted
bullets.body: Everpure (ticker P) reaffirmed FY27 revenue at $5.03-5.07B (in-line) but issued preliminary FY28 guidance of $7.0-7.3B vs. FactSet consensus $6.19B (+13-18% beat) and operating income of $1.7-1.9B vs. consensus $1.32B (+29-44% beat). Two hyperscale customers have firm commitments through FY28; new revenue streams (hyperscale, modern data software, Scale.i) targeting ~20% of total revenue by 2030. FY28 operating margin guided 24-26%.

bullets.title: IONQ +4.4%: Quantum error decoder milestone, QPU debuting at NVDA facility
bullets.body: IonQ announced a quantum error decoder breakthrough and will bring its Superion 256 QPU to Nvidia's Accelerated Quantum Research Center, driving a 4.4% gain. Jefferies corporate access calendar shows an IonQ CFO/COO investor meeting scheduled for Nov 9 in NYC.

bullets.title: MSFT +0.5%: Stifel upgrade; Copilot 30-50% discounts to boost enterprise adoption; $10B+ Middle East AI investment
bullets.body: Microsoft gained 0.5% following a Stifel upgrade and reports it is offering 30-50% discounts on Copilot subscriptions to accelerate enterprise penetration. Separately, MSFT announced $10B+ in UAE/Saudi/Qatar/Kuwait cloud and AI infrastructure investment through 2030, plus ~$400M in subsea/terrestrial connectivity.

bullets.title: NVDA: Jensen Huang bullish on 2+ years of compute supply deficit; China increasingly buying H200s
bullets.body: Nvidia CEO Huang said AI compute demand will outstrip supply for at least two years and dismissed dot-com-style overbuild concerns. A Jefferies expert call noted China is increasingly comfortable purchasing H200 chips as domestic localization confidence grows, and a trade truce extension of 6+ months is likely. GS analyst Jim Schneider maintains Buy on NVDA.

bullets.title: CDNS +2.0%: Expanded TSMC partnership for AI/HPC across N3, N2, A16, A14 processes
bullets.body: Cadence expanded its TSMC collaboration with tool certification for the A14 process, UALink solutions in N3P, and new silicon-proven IP for N3P/N2P. The partnership enables agentic AI chip and 3D-IC design flows; CDNS stock rose $10.75. Berenberg separately called CDNS and SNPS the best investment opportunity in software/IT services, with AI monetization expected from 2027.

bullets.title: PAYX down 8.8%: Management Solutions miss overshadows EPS beat; Wells lowers estimates, keeps Underweight
bullets.body: Paychex fell 8.8% despite Q1 EPS of $1.34 vs. consensus $1.32 as the Management Solutions segment missed. Wells Fargo maintains Underweight: F2Q margins guided down 170bps y/y and MS revenue growth lowered to 4.5% from 5.5% for FY27. ASO-to-PEO conversions ran 2x expectations in F1Q but guidance assumes moderation; Wells cuts FY27/FY28 EPS to $5.93/$6.38 from $5.94/$6.40.

bullets.title: RCL down ~10% post-Sandals: GS sees strategic logic, leverage impact only +0.3x
bullets.body: Royal Caribbean confirmed acquisition of a 50% stake in Sandals Resorts for ~$3B (implying >$6B enterprise value, $500-700M EBITDA pre-synergies). GS argues the sell-off is overdone: net leverage rises only 0.3x within target range, overlapping Caribbean destinations enable vacation wallet capture and cross-sell, and investor feedback was relatively positive on valuation and 2027 setup.

bullets.title: DIS raises Disney+ 13% to $21.49; YouTube launches creator tools to counter Netflix
bullets.body: Disney raised its Disney+ monthly price by 13% to $21.49 effective today. Separately, YouTube is rolling out new creator tools to defend its talent base against Netflix competition.

bullets.title: UBS initiates HUT, WULF, CORZ, CIFR at Buy on data center AI demand thesis
bullets.body: UBS initiated coverage: HUT Buy/$143 (pipeline conversion, high-credit counterparties), WULF Buy/$24 (brownfield conversion for inference workloads), CORZ Buy/$24 (tenant expansion optionality, geographic diversification), CIFR Buy/$23 (discounted near-term leasing). Data center REITs fell 2.13% on the day despite +28% YTD, pressured by Prince William County restrictions and Texas delays.

bullets.title: Wells Fargo bullish on IPPs TLN, CEG, VST; FSLR benefits from DOC anti-stockpiling rule
bullets.body: Wells Fargo sees an IPP valuation inflection weeks away with strong customer demand; price targets TLN $501, CEG $362, VST $212 on FCF yields now in teens. ROTH Capital (Buy, $300 PT) views the DOC anti-stockpiling rule on polysilicon favorably for FSLR, potentially resetting US module ASPs by $0.10-$0.20/watt. Utilities index fell 1.9% on yield surge.

bullets.title: AFRM -5.1%: Higher rates hit BNPL; B. Riley sees open-loop card launch as catalyst
bullets.body: Affirm fell 5.1% as fintech non-bank lenders broadly underperformed in a rising rate environment (10Y hit 5.11%). B. Riley sees a catalyst in BNPL open-loop card launch, which shifts revenue mix from merchant fees toward interchange and subscription fees.

bullets.title: HOOD: Hedgeye initiates slight long bias — cyclical trading engine masked by diversification story
bullets.body: Hedgeye adds HOOD to Long Bench with slight long bias: ~50% of revenue still driven by degenerate trading at 90-100% incremental margins, and event contracts drove nearly half of revenue growth this year. Diversification into crypto, retirement, banking, and tokenization is real but current multiple assumes continued good times rather than a proven secular platform.

bullets.title: CVNA, KMX insulated from Meta Muse auto disintermediation; B2C marketplaces most at risk
bullets.body: JPM argues CVNA's vertical integration (owned inventory, captive finance, 30-second loan origination, reconditioning, logistics) makes it resistant to AI agent displacement; KMX shares similar structural insulation. B2C marketplaces (CARS, CAR) carry the lightest asset footprints and face the most pronounced network-effect erosion as agent adoption expands among dealers and consumers.

bullets.title: SHOP: Meta Muse pressure creates buy opportunity per Mizuho; stock down 7%
bullets.body: Mizuho reiterates Outperform on SHOP, arguing today's 7% decline driven by Meta Pay/Muse headlines is a buying opportunity. Shopify management confirmed to Mizuho that wallets competing for Muse checkout confirm Shopify remains the underlying processing and settlement layer — agentic commerce is a new distribution channel, not disintermediation.

bullets.title: GS Semis: Buy NVDA, AMD, AVGO, CRDO, SNDK, STX; Sell ARM, TXN; Neutral INTC, MRVL, MU
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs analyst Jim Schneider (covering 35+ names) is marketing in NYC on Oct 9; his conviction buys include NVDA, AMD, AVGO, CRDO, SNDK, and STX. Sells are ARM and TXN; Neutrals include INTC, MRVL, MU, and WDC.

bullets.title: Macro: PMI shock sends 10Y to 5.11%, 5Y auction tails 3.2bp — risk-off across tech/semis
bullets.body: September flash composite PMI hit 58.4 (vs 55.3 consensus), highest since 2021, with manufacturing at 57.0. The 5Y Treasury auction tailed 3.2bp — the largest since June 2022 — with end-users awarded only 84.2% (lowest since May 2024). 2Y yields hit +15bps to 4.89%, 10Y at 5.11% (post-GFC high), Nasdaq -1.13%, S&P -0.75%. Fed's Barr signaled further hikes needed.

bullets.title: BABA -4.8%: China probes DeepSeek and Moonshot AI over data security
bullets.body: Alibaba fell 4.8% after China announced probes into DeepSeek and Moonshot AI startups over data security concerns, pressuring Chinese internet names broadly.

bullets.title: TEAM +3.4%: Accelerated IL5 authorization and air-gapped cloud deployment plans
bullets.body: Atlassian gained 3.4% on news of accelerated IL5 government authorization and plans for air-gapped cloud deployment, expanding its federal market addressability.

bullets.title: MSFT: Stifel upgrade drives +0.5%; software outperforms semis on risk-off rotation
bullets.body: Software was the brightest tech subsector (+1.1%) as investors rotated from semis (-1.2%) on AI compute revenue scaling concerns. MSFT +0.5% on Stifel upgrade and Copilot discount strategy; HUBS +3.6% on FBN Securities initiation at Sector Perform with $230 target.
